Final hypothesis (natural-language, 4 sentences) and supporting artefacts ready for review.

ANSWER (verbatim, in submission.answer and payload.hypothesis):
"Under a Firth-penalised logistic specification that adjusts for the academic-performance proxies (ASVAB composite and percentile in class) and the demographic controls (sex and family size), the implied gap in predicted BA-completion probability for Black relative to White respondents is positive at every global SES quartile and monotonically increasing across the SES distribution: approximately +0.06 percentage points in Q1 (lowest SES), +0.08 in Q2, +0.08 in Q3, and +0.09 in Q4 (highest SES). The Black advantage is therefore most pronounced at the top of the SES distribution (Q4), although the absolute magnitude is very small (sub-tenth-of-a-percent) and the 95% confidence interval on every cell spans zero. The unadjusted specification shows the opposite pattern (Black behind White by 1.3 to 3.1 pp at every quartile), so this conditional Black advantage only emerges once the academic-ability controls are partialled out and must be read as a descriptive contrast rather than a causal effect. The Black subsample at Q4 is small (n = 264, 8 BA events), so the precise Q4 magnitude is the least stable of the four estimates."

ARTIFACTS PRODUCED (all in /workspace/artifacts/):
- analysis.py                        (executed; 13.9 KB)
- main.txt                           (full write-up used for the submission)
- summary_table.csv                  (Black/Hispanic/White unadjusted AND adjusted; Firth + MLE)
- cell_table.csv                     (n, BA events, raw rate per race x SES quartile)
- coefficients_adjusted.csv          (Firth + MLE under adjusted model)
- coefficients_unadjusted.csv        (Firth + MLE under race x SES only)
- submission_payload.json            (the structured submission object)

KEY FINDING NUMBERS (Firth ADJUSTED, primary contrast):
  Quartile | Black  | White  | GAP
  Q1       | 0.542% | 0.480% | +0.062 pp
  Q2       | 0.713% | 0.632% | +0.081 pp
  Q3       | 0.738% | 0.654% | +0.084 pp
  Q4       | 0.804% | 0.713% | +0.092 pp   <-- "more pronounced"
Firth UNADJUSTED: Black behind White at every quartile, gaps -1.32 / -3.12 / -2.69 / -2.65 pp.
MLE ADJUSTED (robustness): same direction, same ordering, smaller magnitudes (~+0.00 to +0.01 pp).
Hispanic vs White supplementary gap: monotonic, same direction, larger magnitude (Q1=+0.24 to Q4=+0.36 pp).

BLACK x SES cell sizes (n, BA events): Q1=(682,3) | Q2=(676,9) | Q3=(491,8) | Q4=(264,8).

READY FOR YOUR REVIEW. The actor runtime was well within limits: a single Python script run produced everything in <2 s; no external data, no fabricated statistics. Descriptive language only. Firth used as requested; MLE as one-paragraph robustness. Hispanic included in the table but not in the primary contrast. Global-quartile SES as requested.
